record.original_question: Must every pseudocompact symmetrizable space be first-countable?

evidence.quote:
A space X is symmetrizable if the topology of X is generated by some symmetric

Problem 6. Is every pseudocompact symmetrizable space ﬁrst-countabl e?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A symmetric on a set $X$ is a function $d:X\times X\to[0,\infty)$ such that, for all $x,y\in X$, $d(x,y)=d(y,x)$ and $d(x,y)=0$ if and only if $x=y$. A topological space $(X,\tau)$ is called symmetrizable if there exists a symmetric $d$ on $X$ such that $\tau$ coincides with the topology generated by $d$ in the following sense: a set $U\subseteq X$ is open if and only if for every $x\in U$ there exists $\varepsilon>0$ with $\{y\in X:d(x,y)<\varepsilon\}\subseteq U$. A space $X$ is pseudocompact if it is Tychonoff and every continuous real-valued function on $X$ is bounded. A space $X$ is first-countable if every point has a countable neighborhood base.

Question: Must every pseudocompact symmetrizable space be first-countable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every pseudocompact symmetrizable space must be first-countable is a known open problem in general topology, attributed to Arhangel'skii and listed in collections of selected open problems. A web search did not locate any published resolution; related results address first-countability of symmetrizable spaces under stronger hypotheses (e.g. compactness or Lindelöfness) but not the pseudocompact case.

status_evidence.title: Problems from Topology Proceedings
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of symmetrizable spaces and related open problems by Arhangel'skii.
status_evidence.claim: Open problems on symmetrizable spaces, including their first-countability under various compactness-like hypotheses, are recorded in topology problem collections.

status_evidence.title: On symmetrizability and perfectness of second-countable spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Symmetrizable spaces and their first-countability are studied; second-countable Hausdorff spaces are symmetrizable iff perfect.
status_evidence.claim: Symmetrizability and first-countability remain actively studied, with no resolution of the pseudocompact case located.
